title: Kernel Probe Scheduler and Prefill/Decode Hedging Optimizer
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Current runtime picks kernels per-request using static heuristics that often underperform on mixed-length conversational workloads. Long-prefill bursts and short decode-heavy responses show different optimal kernels; picking one globally increases p95 latency and cost. Goal: Implement a lightweight Kernel Probe Scheduler (KPS) that performs microprobes and schedules kernel choices separately for prefill and decode phases with token-phase aware warmstarts and hedging policies. The scheduler should be safe to run on production traffic, have a small CPU/microbenchmark cost, and reduce p95 latency on mixed workloads while keeping per-token cost within 5% of baseline. Scope: KPS prototype, telemetry hooks, canary rollout, and can be toggled per-customer or per-model. Out of scope: full offline ML model for kernel prediction (we will use heuristics + small bandit sampler in this ticket).
acceptance_criteria: KPS can run per-request and decide separate kernels for prefill vs decode at runtime
Microprobe latency overhead per request <= 1.5ms p50 on x86 control plane and <= 0.8ms p50 on worker-hosted probes
End-to-end p95 latency improvement >= 6% on mixed prefills (seqlen distribution skewed 70/30 long/short) in A/B canary vs baseline
No customer-visible increase in error rate or OOM frequency during canary (compare week-over-week)
Telemetry: per-request kernel choice, probe_result, confidence_score, and hedged_fallback events emitted to runtime-traces
risks_and_mitigation: Probe noise producing unstable kernel oscillation - mitigation: exponential backoff on switches + minimum decision window of 10s per model/route
Probe overhead causing CPU pressure - mitigation: sample rate capped at 1% of traffic, adaptive to worker load metrics
Incorrect kernel choice increases tail latency - mitigation: hedging policy that triggers hot fallback to baseline kernel if p95 exceeds threshold
Compatibility mismatch with quantized kernels on older GPUs - mitigation: catalog compatibility matrix check and fallback to verified quantized variant
implementation_notes: Components: (1) Probe microbench module: runs a tiny pref/dec kernel microcall on a warmed shard (no full model weights, uses representative op sequence) and returns latency/cost estimate. (2) Decision engine: token-phase estimator + bandit sampler that updates kernel weights per (model, route, instance_type, seqlen_bucket). (3) Hedging controller: monitors per-request latency and can spawn parallel fallback decode on lower-latency kernel when tail risk detected. (4) Telemetry: new runtime-traces fields (kps.probe.latency_ms, kps.chosen_kernel, kps.confidence, kps.hedge_triggered). Implementation will be gated behind runtime flag and per-customer opt-in.
tradeoffs_decisions: Decision: Use a lightweight epsilon-greedy bandit with stratification by seqlen_bucket rather than a full contextual bandit — rationale: lower implementation complexity, predictable behavior, and safer initial rollout

Decision: Separate kernel pools for prefill and decode phases rather than trying to find one kernel for whole request — rationale: empirical microbenchmarks show different kernels win depending on whether KV-cache is involved and average decode length
Decision: Limit probe frequency and prefer warmstart probes to avoid cold-start noise — rationale: reduces variance and protects GPU memory bandwidth
rollout_plan: 1) Unit/integration tests + synthetic workload benching on staging. 2) Dogfood on internal models with 0.1% traffic to collect telemetry for 24h. 3) Canary to 5% of production traffic for 72h with automated rollback if p95 latency or error spikes. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% and then full enablement for selected model families. Toggle controls: per-customer config, model label 'kps-enabled', and runtime flag 'kps.global'.
telemetry_and_metrics: Add new dashboards: KPS Probe Overhead (ms), KPS Decision Stability (switches/min), P95 delta (kps vs baseline) per-route, Hedge Trigger Rate, Cost delta per-token. Alerts: rollback if p95 increases > 8% sustained for 15m or if hedge_trigger_rate > 2% of requests.
testing_plan: Microbench suites for representative kernel/seqlen combos. Fuzz tests for token-phase estimation. Load test harness reproducing mixed-traffic (30% short decode, 70% long prefill). Nightly synthetic regression tests run against runtime-1.18 image. End-to-end smoke tests verifying no extra OOMs and correct telemetry emission.

notes_for_sre: SREs: be aware that KPS will emit additional telemetry which could increase event volume. We cap probe sampling to 1% and will coordinate to ensure observability ingestion capacity is sufficient during canary. If memory pressure observed on worker GPUs during warmstart probes, disable KPS via 'kps.global=false' and notify runtime team.
